newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-EDBERG KEEPS ANKLE STRAPPED IN HOPE OF PLAYING.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-EDBERG KEEPS ANKLE STRAPPED IN HOPE OF PLAYING.

text.p: Stefan Edberg, who hobbled to defeat in Friday's opening Davis Cup final singles after twisting his ankle, hopes to resume light training later on Saturday, his doctor said.
Edberg fell awkwardly in the sixth game of his 6-3 6-4 6-3 defeat by France's Cedric Pioline.
He has some ligament damage and swelling in his right ankle, his doctor, Nils Westlin, said.
The Swedish winner of six grand slam titles, who retires after this weekend's final, kept his foot tightly bandaged after x-rays were taken.
He is scheduled to meet Arnaud Boetsch in the final reverse singles on Sunday. If he is not fit his place will be taken by Jonas Bjorkman or Nicklas Kulti who were playing doubles on Saturday.
Swedish team officials said it was unlikely any decision on Edberg's fitness would be made until just before Sunday's matches.
